title: The ringing beside the step

data.source: Cut times of the printed rotor (section IV) and of a toy path that steps back, rebuilt from 50, 200 and 800 Fourier harmonics.

prediction: Rebuilt from finitely many waves, the count staircase overshoots by 0.0895 of the jump beside every cut, however many waves are used, and by the same amount whether or not the path had surplus.
baseline: The Wilbraham-Gibbs overshoot of a Fourier series at a jump, and Fejer averaging, which removes it.
why: P2 to P4 held. P1 held at 200 and 800 waves but missed its 0.002 tolerance at 50 waves, where the neighbouring cut still ripples. The overshoot is a fact about adding up waves, known since 1848. It is the same with and without surplus, so it says nothing about the system. CRR adds no prediction here.
